issues.legal_issue: An expectant Muslim heir may be estopped from claiming an inheritance that later vests when the heir’s relinquishment for consideration forms part of conduct that induced others to act to their detriment.
material_facts: Before their father’s death, two sons executed deeds acknowledging receipt of cash and movable property in return for not claiming future rights in specified properties.
The other sons relied on the deeds and the relinquishing sons’ conduct, and paid the father’s debts, thereby preserving the estate.
The relinquishing sons did not object during their father’s lifetime, when he could have disposed of the properties and defeated their expectations of inheritance.
After their father died and inheritance rights vested, the two sons sought partition of the properties covered by the deeds.
issues.conclusion: The sons were estopped from claiming the inherited shares covered by the deeds; the appeal was allowed and the first appellate court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Evidence Act, 1872 permits equitable estoppel, as a rule of evidence, to prevent assertion of an otherwise existing right when a person’s declarations or conduct induced another to act. Muslim law’s rule that an expectant heir cannot transfer a spes successionis (comparable in effect to section 6(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882) makes the purported transfer ineffective, but does not prohibit conduct that may create an estoppel; section 23 of the Contract Act, 1872 therefore does not bar the estoppel. Latafat Hussain v. Hidayat Hussain, AIR 1936 All 573, was approved; Abdul Kafoor v. Abdul Razack, AIR 1959 Mad 131, and Asa Beevi v. Karuppan, (1918) 41 Mad ILR 365, were disapproved. The court found it unnecessary to decide whether there was a technical family settlement.

predicates.inheritance_partition_claim: A claimant sought partition of property on the basis of an inheritance that had vested.
predicates.prospective_heirs_relinquished_expected_: Before the ancestor’s death, prospective heirs declared that they would not claim specified property and received consideration for that declaration.
predicates.other_family_members_relied_by_preservin: Other family members relied on the declarations and conduct by paying debts or otherwise preserving the estate.
predicates.prospective_heirs_later_claimed_the_shar: After the inheritance vested, the prospective heirs claimed the shares they had earlier disclaimed.

issues.definition: When prospective heirs accept consideration for disclaiming expected shares, other family members rely on that conduct to preserve the estate, and the heirs later claim those shares in a partition proceeding, the claim is barred by estoppel.
